language.description:
The UI language: one of `rb_i18n::available_locales()` (only `en` in phase 1,
RB-010-14).

theme.description: Light, dark or follow the system (RB-010-07).

visible.description:
Show the status bar at the bottom of the window; hidden, the grid takes its room and the
messages still reach the history.

infoTimeoutSec.description:
How long an info or success message stays in the bar, in seconds; 0 keeps it until the
next one. Warnings and errors stay until closed.

historySize.description: How many messages the history keeps, oldest dropped first.

canvasZoom.description:
Show the canvas zoom at the right of the status bar while the canvas layout is shown: the
active view's page zoom, a slider, the minus and plus buttons and the presets (RB-080-94).

highlightActiveView.description:
The label strip of the active view (the leader) is drawn in the accent colour, in every
layout with label strips - grid, focus, horizontal, split; the canvas board marks it
itself (RB-080-04).

pageContextMenu.description:
The page's context menu offers rBrowser's block below Chromium's entries: Inspect
element, DevTools, Screenshot, Video, Checks and Panels for the clicked view
(RB-080-43). Off leaves Chromium's menu and "Do not sync the next click"; the commands
and their chords stay.

viewContextMenu.description:
The menus of the views (RB-080-41): on a view's label strip (the active view's click, a
right-click on the canvas board's label) "Remove view", "Set as active", "Size", the
engine, "Pop out"; on the free canvas, an empty cell or the toolbar's "+" the hidden
breakpoints to add. Off leaves the strips and the canvas as before; the "+" button, the
commands, the palette and MCP stay.

visible.description:
Show the breakpoint bar under every view (formerly the footer), in the breakpoint's
colour, in every layout and in a view's own window; the view gives it 18 px of its height.
Off gives the height back.

items.description: One field of the breakpoint bar. The order of the variants is the order in the strip.

oneOf.description: The widths the breakpoint stands for (`768-1023px`).
The view's width, height and pixel ratio (`768 x 1024 @2x`).

The page's `min-width` / `max-width` conditions that hold at the view's width, from the
analysis of the page; the ends of the breakpoint's range until one ran.
The framework's name for the width (`md`), when the analyser recognised one.

fields.description:
What the breakpoint bar names, in this order: `breakpoint`, `range`, `size`, `queries`,
`framework`; `range` and `framework` by default. A breakpoint bar with no field left is
not shown.

analyze.description:
Read the media queries of the page a view shows from the loaded page itself, after
every load - nothing is requested again - so the breakpoint bar names the page's own
`min-width` / `max-width` queries. Off, the breakpoint bar names the ends of the
breakpoint's range, or what Analyze Breakpoints found.

oneOf.description: A second line when one does not hold the text, broken between two fields.
Always one line; what does not fit is cut at the end.

wrap.description:
What the breakpoint bar does in a view too narrow for its text: `auto` breaks it into a
second line between two fields, and the view gives the breakpoint bar 36 px while it has
two lines; `never` keeps one line that ends in an ellipsis. What is cut is in the tooltip.

oneOf.description: In the middle of the strip, every line.

align.description:
Where the breakpoint bar's text stands in the strip: `center` in the middle of every line,
`start` at the left edge.

vitals.description:
Show the vitals bar under every view, below the breakpoint bar, in every layout and in a
view's own window: the view's Core Web Vitals (LCP, CLS, INP), each with the shape of its
rating, and a warning when the view uses much CPU or memory; the tooltip has all five
vitals with their ratings in words, and a click marks the element behind the worst rated
one. Needs `vitals.enabled` (or `resources.enabled` for the warning); the view gives it
18 px of its height, off gives it back. MCP's `view_metrics` reads the vitals either way.

lighthouse.description:
Show the Lighthouse bar under every view, below the vitals bar, in every layout and in a
view's own window: the four category scores (Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices,
SEO) of the newest Lighthouse run of the page the view shows at its breakpoint, each with
Lighthouse's colour and the shape of its rating; the tooltip names the run's time, a click
opens its report. A view without such a run has no Lighthouse bar; the view gives it 18 px
of its height, off gives it back. MCP's `lighthouse_reports` reads the scores either way.

viewFooter.description: Layout > the breakpoint bar under every view (RB-080-44).

pageContextMenuEmulation.description:
The page's context menu offers the toolbar's emulation switches for the clicked view -
colour scheme, reduced motion, offline, location, time zone, reset - in an Emulation
submenu (RB-080-49). Off, the submenu is gone. Needs `ui.pageContextMenu`.

devices.description:
The "New size..." picker lists the device presets (the built-in ones and your own,
with their pixel ratio) below the sizes. Off leaves the sizes and "Custom...".

newViewSize.description: Layout > what the "New size..." picker lists (RB-080-46).

oneOf.description: One row; what does not fit is in the overflow menu.
Up to two rows; only what a second row does not hold either is in the overflow menu.

overflow.description:
What the toolbar does with the controls a narrow window has no room for: `menu` moves
them into the "More" menu at its right end, `wrap` breaks the toolbar into a second row
and the views move down. The address bar and back, forward and reload always stay.

panelsToggle.description:
Shows the switch of the plugin panels at the right end of the toolbar (RB-080-79): it
opens the docked panels and folds them to their icon rail again. Off by default
(RB-090-10): the panels open from their rail beside the views, the commands and
`Leader P Z`.

portalButton.description:
Shows the portal's button in the toolbar (RB-090-62): off, a click starts the portal and
shows a pairing QR code; on, a menu with the QR code, the devices, a device to disconnect
and the stop, the number of paired devices on the button. Off, the portal still runs from
the Portal panel, the command palette and `Leader S P`.

toolbar.description: The toolbar in a narrow window (RB-080-52) and its optional buttons.

syntaxHighlight.description:
Code shows in syntax colours wherever rBrowser shows it - the plugin panels' values,
stack traces, request and response bodies and headers, snippets and storage values, and
the settings window's JSON view (RB-080-65). Off, code is one colour; more than 200 KiB is
always one colour.

oneOf.description: The active view of the grid.
Ask on every link: the system browser or the active view.

openLinksIn.description:
Where a link from rBrowser's own surfaces opens - a finding's help page, a plugin panel's
report or help link: `system` the default browser, `activeView` the grid's active view,
`ask` asks on every link (RB-080-92).

followWindowsTextSize.description:
rBrowser's own windows - the toolbar, status bar, label strips, breakpoint bars, settings,
palette and panels - grow with Windows' text size (Settings > Accessibility > Text size,
100 to 225 %) and follow a change at once (RB-090-26). Off keeps them at 100 %. The
pages in the views are never affected; their zoom is the page zoom.

position.description:
Where the bar stands while something runs: `top`, below the toolbar, or `bottom`, above
the status bar. The views give it its height and take it back when the last activity
ends.

oneOf.description: The bar always, empty while nothing runs: the views keep their place (RB-094-13).
The bar with the running activities' controls, only while something runs.
No bar; the toolbar's compact indicators only.

mode.description:
`always` keeps the bar's room, empty while nothing runs, so the views never move; `bar`
shows the bar only while something runs; `indicator` draws no bar and leaves each
activity to its compact indicator in the toolbar.

video.description: A video recording: its time, the views recorded and Stop.

recorder.description: A recording of steps: its steps, Pause or Resume, Stop, Add check and Play last.

flows.description: A flow run, a recording played back included: the views through, Cancel and Results.

checks.description: A check run, Lighthouse included: its progress and Cancel.

portal.description: The running portal: its devices, a new QR code and Disconnect.

desync.description: Views out of sync: how many, and Resync.

time.description:
The page clock or the animations changed (RB-094-07): the time and rate, Step, Real
time and 100 %.

plugins.description:
A plugin call that reports its progress (RB-093-01): the plugin, how far it is and
Cancel when the plugin has a cancel command.

forcedStates.description: Pseudo-class states forced on an element (RB-094-16): the states, the views and Reset.

show.description:
Which activities have an entry in the bar; one switched off shows only its compact
indicator in the toolbar.

activityBar.description: The activity bar while something runs, its place and its entries (RB-090-67).

engineStatus.description:
The label strip of a Firefox or WebKit view says how its engine's window stands
(starting, in its cell, engine stopped, ...), in the engine badge beside the engine's
name (`Firefox · window closed`), the reason in the tooltip; the badge's menu then offers
to restart a stopped engine or bring its window to the front. Off, the engine badge and
MCP's `views_list` still name the engine.

oneOf.description: While the view's address is not the active view's.

address.description:
When the label strip shows the view's address: `differs` while it is not the active
view's address (a view with its own navigation, sync off, a view that could not follow),
`always` for every view, `off` never.

addressEditable.description:
A click on the address in the label strip of a view with its own navigation (decoupled
with `Leader S U` or `syncNavigation: false`) opens an address field there, as does
`view.edit_address` (`Leader S L`): Enter loads the address in that view only, Escape
cancels (RB-092-03). Off, the address only shows and its click makes the view active.

cellLabel.description: Layout > what each view's label strip shows beside its name (RB-090-27).

oneOf.description: The system's local time, daylight saving time included.

fileNameTime.description: Local time or UTC in the folder and file names a person reads (RB-090-69).

firstRunWizard.description:
The setup wizard (RB-091-05) opens by itself at the very first start, and a project
folder without a config says "Set up project" once in the status bar. Off: neither, and
the command that opens the wizard refuses - for a team that rolls out its own setup.

showVersion.description: The main window's title shows rBrowser's version after its name, as About shows it.

showCredit.description:
The main window's title ends in the credit line "made with Love by Alexander
Herling/DEGOYA.digital".

titleBar.description:
What the main window's title shows after the project and the product: the version and
the credit line (RB-094-19).

errorToast.description:
The error of an action you started - adding a device, starting a view, a menu row or a
toolbar button that failed - shows at the top of the window as well, in the toolbar's
strip, never over the views, with the message's buttons (Settings, Retry, Download).
Off: the status bar alone.

notifications.description: Layout > Status bar: an action's error at the top as well (RB-094-20).

recentProjects.description: General > recent projects, newest first (absolute paths).

openLastProject.description:
Started without a project (and none found upwards): open the newest of
`recentProjects`.

focusOnOpen.description:
The window takes the focus when a project opens or a second call hands it a URL;
`--background` overrides it for one call.

oneOf.description: The project's start URL (`startUrl`) in every view.
The page each view showed when rBrowser last closed, in the environment in effect.

restore.description:
What the views open when the project opens (RB-092-04): `startUrl`, the project's start
URL, or `last`, the page each view showed when rBrowser last closed (kept only in the
project's browser profile). A URL on the command line always wins.

fitToWindow.description:
After a layout change (a layout preset, focus mode, the project opening or its config
changing), views zoomed by hand go back to their cell's zoom; off, they keep it. An
environment change leaves the zoom alone.

defaultZoom.description:
The zoom of the cells rBrowser lays out itself (no `layout.cells` in the config, the
focus-mode view): `"fit"` or a factor `0.25`..=`1`; cells of the config keep their own.

grid.description: Layout > zoom of the grid area (RB-010-12).

arrowKeys.description: Left and right arrow switch the breakpoint while the shell has the focus.

keepFocus.description:
A page loading in the focus view (each arrow key opens the next breakpoint's view) leaves
the keyboard focus where it is, so the toolbar's next arrow key steps again. Off: the
view takes the focus, as a page does after a navigation.

jsonHighlight.description:
The JSON view colours keys, strings, numbers, booleans, `null` and punctuation, in both
themes; off, the text is one colour. Copy delivers plain JSON either way.

showKeys.description:
Every setting prints its key (`updates.channel`) under its title. Off, the key is in the
title's tooltip and behind the copy button that appears on the row; the search finds a
setting by its key either way (RB-080-70).

sectionTabs.description:
A category with more than one section shows one section per tab; the search, "Only
changed" and a link to a setting reach every tab. Off, every section of a category stands
on one page (RB-080-71).

settings.description: General > appearance: the settings window's JSON view (RB-080-42).

snap.description:
Canvas: a moved view snaps to this grid in DIP (0 for none) and to the edges of views
closer than it, unless the preset sets its own `snap`.

minimap.description:
Canvas: the minimap in the toolbar strip shows every view and the visible area; a click
centres the canvas on that point.

oneOf.description: At the end of the toolbar, before the menus.
At the start of the toolbar, after the logo.

minimapPosition.description: Canvas: the minimap's place in the toolbar strip.

horizontalHeight.description:
Horizontal: the row height when the preset sets none - `"fit"` (the grid area's) or a
height in DIP.

splitStep.description:
Split: how far one keyboard step moves the divider, as a share of the area (0.01 to
0.25).

spacePan.description:
Canvas: Space held turns any drag on the canvas board - a view's label too - into a pan;
a drag on the empty board always pans.

oneOf.description: `config.json`: checked in, shared with the team.

savePresetTo.description:
The file "Save layout as preset" writes when the call names none: `local`
(`config.local.json`, personal) or `project` (`config.json`, shared with the team).

wheelZoom.description:
Canvas: Ctrl + mouse wheel over the canvas board - the free area or a view's label -
zooms the canvas around the pointer; the views grow and shrink with it. Off: the wheel
does nothing there. Over a view the page zooms, as in every layout.

middleButtonPan.description:
Canvas: the middle mouse button held and dragged pans the canvas, as Space + drag does -
over a view, a label or a breakpoint bar too, where the page's autoscroll does not start
then. Off gives the middle button back to the pages.

showPartialViews.description:
Canvas: a view that reaches past the edge of the grid area shows the part of its page
that lies inside; only a view wholly outside is hidden and paused. Off: a view is hidden
as soon as any part of it leaves the area.

layoutModes.description: Layout > further modes: horizontal, split and canvas (RB-080-04).

keepPlaceholder.description:
The grid keeps the popped-out view's cell with a placeholder (a click brings the window
to the front); off, the other views close the gap.

fitToScreen.description:
A window larger than the screen is cut to it and the page shown at a zoom below 1, named
in the title; off, the window keeps the real size beyond the screen.

rememberBounds.description: Each breakpoint's window opens where and as large as it was last closed.

popOut.description: Layout > pop-out: a view in a window of its own at its real size (RB-080-14).

throttleHidden.description:
A view without area on screen is reported hidden to Chromium, which stops painting it
and throttles its timers; navigation and scroll sync still reach it, and it catches up
with the leader's URL and scroll position when it shows again. Off, such views keep
rendering.

inactiveFps.description:
Visible views that are not the active one run with their main thread slowed to about
this many frames per second of work (CDP CPU throttling, 60 / value); 0 (or 60) leaves
them at full speed. Sync still reaches them, a little later.

memoryWarningMb.description:
The shell warns once when rBrowser's processes together use more private memory than
this many MiB; 0 turns the warning off.

counters.description:
The timing counters of the sync hub, the plugin calls and the shell IPC record (RB-090-32):
the MCP tool `app_perf` and the diagnostics ZIP (`perf.json`) read them. Off, nothing is
recorded; what was recorded stays readable.

performance.description:
Layout > grid and Advanced > experimental flags: throttling and the memory warning
(RB-020-09).

port.description: A fixed port; random when absent.

allowEvaluate.description: The `evaluate` tool may run page JavaScript.

port.description: A fixed port on 127.0.0.1; a free one at every start when absent (RB-030-01).

navigationTimeoutMs.description:
How long MCP waits for each view, in milliseconds: the final URL of `navigate`,
`reload`, `back` and `forward`, the input of `click`, `type`, `hover` and `press_key`,
and `sync_set`'s work (RB-030-01).

consoleLogLimit.description: Console messages kept per view for `console_logs` (RB-030-01).

networkRequestLimit.description: Network requests kept per view for `network_requests` (RB-030-01).

errorLimit.description: Uncaught exceptions kept per view for `errors` (RB-030-01).

collectNetwork.description:
Network requests are collected from the start; off, from the first time they are asked
for (`network_requests`, a plugin's network list) (RB-090-34).

maxAnswerBytes.description: The most bytes `evaluate` and `snapshot` answer; more is cut (RB-030-01).

stdioAutoStart.description:
`rbrowser mcp` starts the project's rBrowser in the background when none runs
(RB-030-02).

notifyOnSettingChange.description: A setting changed over MCP is shown in the shell (RB-030-03).

prompts.description:
The server offers its prompts, the workflows `responsive_review`, `a11y_triage` and
`bug_repro` (RB-095-01).

resources.description:
The server offers its read-only resources: `rbrowser://views`, the latest findings and
screenshots, the project config (RB-095-01).

client.description:
The AI client the MCP setup shows first, in the setup wizard and in Settings >
Automation > MCP (RB-091-09).

enabled.description:
The portal may run. Off, `portal.toggle` refuses; on, the portal still listens only once a
person starts it (MCP cannot).

interface.description:
The IPv4 address of the LAN interface the portal listens on; empty: the interface of the
default route, and only when its address is private (RFC 1918, 169.254/16, 100.64/10) -
a public or VPN address refuses to start. Never every interface (`0.0.0.0`).

port.description: A fixed port; a free one at every start when absent.

pairingTtlSec.description: How long the pairing code in the QR code stays valid, in seconds.

maxDevices.description: How many devices may be paired at once.

offerAssetOrigins.description:
When a portal page names a local origin (`http://localhost:5173`) the shown environment
does not list in `assetOrigins`, the status bar offers to add it; a person's click writes
the project config. Off, the log names the origin only (RB-090-71).

enabled.description:
A presentation over the internet may run. Off, `portal.present.start` refuses; on, it
still starts only when a person runs it (MCP cannot).

consented.description:
The person agreed that the presentation's traffic runs through Cloudflare (a Quick
Tunnel, meant for tests and demonstrations). Set by the consent in the Portal panel.

linkTtlSec.description: How long a viewer link stays valid, in seconds. Each link works once.

maxViewers.description: How many viewers may watch at once.

allowPaths.description:
The paths a viewer may load (`/shop` allows `/shop` and everything below it). Empty: the
shown environment's start page and everything below it.

denyPaths.description:
Paths a viewer never loads, even below an allowed one: they answer 404 and never reach
the dev server (`/admin` also covers `/admin/users` and `/administrator`).

pointer.description: A short flash on the viewer's page where the presenter clicks.

presentation.description: The portal shown over the internet through a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel (RB-096-05).

portal.description: Security & Privacy > Portal: devices in the LAN (RB-080-05).

dir.description:
The folder of the flows, relative to the project; `.rbrowser/flows` or a folder inside it,
which workspace trust covers.

parallel.description: How many views run a flow at once; 0 runs all at once.

timeoutMs.description: How long a flow may run in one view, in milliseconds.

actionTimeoutMs.description:
How long one action of a flow (a click, a fill, a wait for an element) may wait, in
milliseconds, before it fails with its locator; never longer than the flow may run
(RB-090-76).

syncDuringRun.description:
Keep syncing input between the views while a flow runs; off, the views of the run
stop syncing until it ends (otherwise each action happens twice).

screenshotOnFailure.description: Save a screenshot of a view whose flow failed or timed out.

oneOf.description:
The run plays in the views shown; the hidden ones and the breakpoints the flow names that
no view shows are named as skipped in the result and a notice.
The run shows the layout `runLayout` while it goes on, and the one before after it.

hiddenViews.description:
What a run does with views the layout hides: `skip` plays in the views shown and names the
rest, `layout` shows `runLayout` for the run (RB-090-84).

revealRecording.description:
With `hiddenViews: skip`, a played recording whose views the layout all hides brings the
first into sight - the canvas centred on it, the strip scrolled to it, focus mode on its
breakpoint - instead of failing (RB-090-89). Off, it fails as any run with no view shown.

confirmDelete.description:
"Delete" in the Flows panel asks in the panel before the flow's file is deleted
(RB-090-91). Off, a click deletes it at once.

runLayout.description:
The layout a run shows with `hiddenViews: layout`: `grid`, `horizontal`, `split` or
`canvas` over the preset shown, or a preset's id.
The settings window offers the modes and the project's presets (source `layouts`).

flows.description: Flows: Playwright scripts of the project that run in every view (RB-040-07).

sandbox.description:
Run the Chromium processes in the sandbox (ADR 0001, Decision 6). Off only where the
sandbox fails on a machine; read at start-up, and while it is off the log says so at
every start. `--no-sandbox` on the command line switches it off for one start.

enabled.description:
Load the extensions below into the Chromium views. Off loads none; the list is kept.
The change takes effect at the next start.

offerProjectRecommendations.description:
A trusted project's recommended extensions (`extensions` in its config) are offered in a
notice; they are added only by the command Extensions: add the project's
recommendations, never by themselves.

path.description:
The absolute path of the extension's folder (the one holding `manifest.json`); a path
to the `manifest.json` itself names its folder.

enabled.description: Load this extension at the next start.

unpacked.description:
Unpacked extensions: each a folder with a Manifest V3 `manifest.json`, referenced where
it is, not copied. Changes take effect at the next start.

allowWebStore.description:
Extensions from the Chrome Web Store (an id or a store URL) may be installed: downloaded
from Google's update server, their CRX3 signatures checked, unpacked under rBrowser's
local folder and loaded like an unpacked folder. Off hides the field and refuses the
commands; what is installed stays loaded.

chromium.description: Chromium, the engine of the grid (RB-010-04).

nodePath.description: A Node runtime of one's own instead of the bundled one.

nodeRpcTimeoutMs.description:
How long a request to the Node sidecar waits for its answer, in milliseconds; a request
that takes longer is cancelled (RB-040-03).

playwrightBrowsersPath.description:
The folder of the Playwright browsers (WebKit); `%LOCALAPPDATA%\rBrowser\ms-playwright`
when absent (RB-040-03).

lighthouseBrowserPath.description:
The Chromium-based browser Lighthouse runs in; absent, an installed one is found
(RB-080-58).

placement.description:
Where a new external window goes: `beside` the main window, on `monitor:<n>` (1-based),
or where it was last (`remember`); further windows cascade.

restartOnCrash.description:
An external window whose engine crashed starts again by itself with its last page, at
most three times in a row with a growing wait; a window you closed stays closed until
you open it again (RB-080-38; `autoRestart` before 0.8).

showTiles.description: The grid shows each external view's status with the buttons "Show window" and "Restart".

embed.description:
A Firefox or WebKit view sits in its grid cell like a Chromium view: its window is owned
by the main window, has no frame, tabs or address bar and follows the cell (RB-080-39).
Off (the default since the owner's test of 2026-11-13: the window shows the page at
100 % cut to the cell, and WebKit's shell keeps its chrome), every such view is a window
of its own beside the main window.

scaleToCell.description:
A view in its cell shows its page at the breakpoint's width scaled to the cell, as a
Chromium view does (RB-080-40): WebKit through its context's scale factor, every
Firefox view at the one factor of the profile. Off, the page is shown at 100 % and cut
to the cell. Nothing without `embed`.

external.description: The external windows of Firefox and WebKit views (RB-040-01).

path.description:
The Firefox executable; found automatically when empty (the registry's App Paths entry,
then the Mozilla Firefox folder under Program Files or the local app data).

syncSource.description:
The Firefox windows are a sync source too: a click in one makes it the active view and
the other views follow it.

extraPrefs.description:
Extra Firefox prefs written to the profile's `user.js` at every start, name to `true`,
`false`, an integer or a string - for what WebDriver BiDi cannot emulate per view
(`ui.prefersReducedMotion: 1`). The remote agent's `remote.*` prefs are refused.

enabled.description:
Breakpoints on WebKit open in a WebKit window (Playwright's WebKit build, not Safari);
off, they stay with Chromium. `engine.webkit.toggle` switches it for the session.

syncSource.description:
Input in a WebKit window is synced to the other views while it is the active view;
off, WebKit windows only follow.

enabled.description:
Breakpoints on Safari open in a Safari window on macOS (the installed Safari, driven by
`safaridriver`); off, they stay with Chromium. Without macOS Safari is not available.

technologyPreview.description:
Safari Technology Preview instead of Safari, when it is installed (its own
`safaridriver`, which needs `--enable` once as well).

mode.description:
Where an iOS view runs: the simulator when Xcode is installed, else a connected device
(`auto`); only the iOS Simulator (`simulator`, needs Xcode); only a connected iPhone or
iPad (`device`).

defaultSimulator.description: The simulator model an iOS breakpoint without `iosDevice` runs on (`iPhone 16`).

bootTimeoutSec.description: How long a simulator may take to boot, in seconds.

ios.description: iOS over `safaridriver`: the Simulator or a connected device, macOS only (RB-095-04).

copy.description:
When the cookies are copied: by hand (`manual`, the command "Copy cookies"), into each
Firefox or WebKit view as it starts (`onStart`), or after each page load of a Chromium
view into the Firefox and WebKit views of its session (`onNavigate`).

domainFilter.description:
Which cookies: those of the sites the views show and of the current environment
(`environment`), or every cookie of the session (`all`).

exclude.description:
Cookies never copied: a cookie name (`*` matches any text, `_ga*`) or a domain, which
covers its subdomains (`tracker.example`).

reload.description: The Firefox and WebKit views that got cookies load their page again, so it sees them.

cookies.description: Copying Chromium's cookies into the Firefox and WebKit views (RB-040-05).

enabled.description:
An Android device on USB can be added as a view: Chrome on the device over ADB, its
DevTools port forwarded to 127.0.0.1 only. The view has the device's own size. Off by
default.

adbPath.description:
The adb executable; found automatically when empty (PATH, ANDROID_HOME,
ANDROID_SDK_ROOT, the usual SDK folders, then the Platform Tools rBrowser downloaded
after you agreed).

reverseLocalhost.description:
A view that loads localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1 reaches that port of this computer: rBrowser
sets `adb reverse` for exactly that port while the view runs and removes it afterwards.
While it stands, other apps on the device can reach that one port too. Off, the device
reaches only itself at a loopback address. On by default.

android.description: Chrome on an Android device over ADB (RB-095-02).

oneOf.description: A window of its own (`show_dev_tools`, the native frontend).

followActiveView.description:
Docked DevTools follow the active view; off, they stay with the view they were opened
for.

dockHeight.description:
The height of DevTools docked below the grid, in DIP; the splitter sets it. The grid
keeps at least a quarter of the window.

dockWidth.description: The width of DevTools docked beside the grid, in DIP; the splitter sets it.

screencast.description:
The hosted frontend's screencast beside the panels (the inspected page once more, in
DevTools' own picture). Off, the panels take the whole dock and inspect mode picks in
the view itself (RB-080-21).

openOnInspect.description:
"Inspect element" (the page's context menu, the shortcut) opens DevTools for the view
when they are closed or with another view, then selects the element. Off, it selects
only in DevTools already open for that view. MCP's `devtools_inspect_at` always opens.

enabled.description: Measure the Web Vitals of every view and show them as badges in the cell label.

poor.description: The highest value that only needs improvement.
The highest value that only needs improvement.
The highest value that only needs improvement.
The highest value that only needs improvement.
The highest value that only needs improvement.

thresholds.description: The rating thresholds per metric; web.dev's by default.

vitals.description: DevTools & Debugging > Web Vitals & resources: the badges and thresholds (RB-060-10).

enabled.description: Read each view's CPU share and memory and show them in the cell label.

ramWarnMb.description: A view whose memory is above this many MB warns.

cpuWarnPercent.description: A view whose CPU share stays above this percentage for five seconds warns.

resources.description: DevTools & Debugging > Web Vitals & resources: CPU and memory per view (RB-060-10).

oneOf.description:
The probe looks for the framework in every page; once it is found, the view offers the
DevTools and the hook goes into the view's next document (reload the view once).

The hook goes into every document of every view before the page's own scripts, so
the DevTools connect without a reload.
Nothing is injected and nothing is offered.

vue.description:
Vue DevTools (Vue 3, `@vue/devtools-kit`). A production build shows its components only
when it is built with `__VUE_PROD_DEVTOOLS__`; the panel says so.

oneOf.description:
The probe looks for the framework in every page; once it is found, the view offers the
DevTools and the hook goes into the view's next document (reload the view once).

The hook goes into every document of every view before the page's own scripts, so
the DevTools connect without a reload.
Nothing is injected and nothing is offered.

react.description:
React DevTools (`react-devtools-inline`): components, props, hooks and the profiler.
React registers with the hook only when the hook is there before React loads, so a view
opened before the hook needs one reload.

frameworkDevtools.description:
DevTools & Debugging > Framework DevTools: the Vue and React DevTools backends in the
views' pages (RB-080-24).

pollingFallback.description: Poll instead of relying on file events.

pollIntervalMs.description: How often polling looks for changes, in milliseconds (RB-030-05).

intervalPauseSec.description: How long input in a view pauses the interval reload, in seconds (RB-030-05).

enabled.description: Self-update at all: off, nothing is fetched and nothing installed (RB-090-02, RB-090-14).

oneOf.description: The build's own: beta for a pre-release build, stable otherwise (RB-090-14).

check.description: When to look for an update (RB-090-02).

autoInstall.description: When a downloaded update installs by itself (RB-090-02).

cefAgeWarning.description:
A notice when the bundled CEF is older than six weeks (RB-010-10); silent while updates
are checked (RB-090-14).

updates.description: General > updates (inactive until the move to GitHub, RB-090-02).

leaderTimeoutMs.description:
How long the leader waits for the next key, in ms; `0` (the default): until `Escape` or
the next key, the which-key bar staying up (RB-080-18).

disableInDevtools.description: rBrowser's shortcuts are off while DevTools have focus.

bindings.description:
The user's bindings by command id, in the text form of `rb-commands`; they replace the
command's defaults. An empty list unbinds the command.

anyOf.description:
`breakpointShortcuts.newViewModifier`. No `Alt`: with the `Ctrl` of a breakpoint key it is
AltGr on German, French and Spanish keyboards; no `Win`: Windows keeps it.

newViewModifier.description:
A modifier (`Shift` or `Ctrl`) that, held with a breakpoint shortcut that does not
contain it already (a project's own `shortcut`) or with a click in the size quick pick,
opens a new view instead of changing the active one.

overlayMs.description: How long the overlay naming the breakpoint stays, in ms.

recentCount.description: How many recently used entries the palette lists first; 0 keeps no history.

showDescriptions.description: The palette shows the description of the selected entry.

prefixes.description:
`>` lists only commands, `@` only views, `#` only settings; off, they are searched as
text.

replaceDefaults.description: `true`: `items` replace the built-in list; `false`: they are added (same id wins).

items.description:
A device preset: the built-in list `crates/rb-config/data/devices.json` (RB-010-12) and the
user's own (`devices` in the user settings). `x-new` is the entry "Add" starts in the
settings: an allowed `kind` and a viewport and pixel ratio `effective_devices` takes (RB-090-61).

label.description: The display name; built-in presets use an i18n key (`devices.<id>`) instead.

kind.description: Mobile, tablet or desktop: groups the quick pick.

items.description:
The presets. A breakpoint whose `device` names a preset takes its viewport, pixel ratio,
user agent, platform and touch for every field it leaves out; what the breakpoint sets
itself wins (RB-010-12). Picking a preset for the active view sizes it to the viewport
(RB-010-16).

defaultGeolocation.description: The geolocation preset (built in or your own) the shortcut sets on a view without one.

id.description: Unique among the presets (`office`); a built-in id is replaced by yours.

label.description: The name shown; built-in presets use an i18n key instead.

geolocationPresets.description: Your own geolocation presets, offered beside Berlin, New York, Tokyo and Sydney.

defaultTimezone.description: The IANA time zone the shortcut sets on a view without one.

defaultCpuThrottling.description: The CPU throttling factor the shortcut sets on a view without one.

factor.description: How much longer a text gets: 1.4 makes it 40 % longer, as German or Finnish often are.

accents.description:
Letters are swapped for accented ones (an `a` gets an acute accent), so a font without
them shows.

rtl.description: The texts also run right to left (Unicode bidi override), as an RTL language would.

pseudoLocale.description: The pseudo-localisation of the page's texts (RB-092-02).

default.description:
The date and time the clock shortcut sets in every view: `2026-12-24T10:00` is each
page's local time, `2026-12-24T10:00:00Z` or with an offset one moment for all; empty
for the moment the shortcut is pressed.

speed.description: How fast that clock runs: 0 holds it fixed, 1 is real time, 60 a minute per second.

clock.description: The page clock the clock shortcut sets in every view (RB-094-07).

animationRates.description: The animation rates the animations shortcut steps through: 0 stops them, 1 is normal.

animationStepMs.description: How far one step moves stopped animations on, in milliseconds.

emulation.description:
Emulation > geolocation, time zone and CPU: the shortcuts' values and own presets
(RB-080-10).

level.description:
The level of the log file: `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug` or `trace` (`RUST_LOG`, when
set, wins).

maxFileSizeMb.description: The size in MiB at which the log file rotates.

maxFiles.description: The log files kept, the current one included.

crashDumpsInBundle.description: The newest crash dumps the diagnostics bundle takes; 0 takes none.

items.description: A plugin id: lower-case words joined by `-` (`overlay-grid`).

disabled.description:
The ids of the plugins switched off. The settings window offers the installed plugins
by name (`x-options`, RB-080-72).

keyId.description: The key's id as the package names it.

publicKey.description: The public key (PEM or base64, as `rb-plugin-pack` writes it).

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the public key, lower-case hex.

trustedKeys.description: The signing keys trusted on first use (pinned by fingerprint).

developmentMode.description: Load unsigned plugins from the plugin folders (development only).

crashLimit.description: Failures after which a plugin is suspended until it is resumed.

compileCache.description: Keep the compiled plugins on disk between starts.

items.description: A plugin id: lower-case words joined by `-` (`overlay-grid`).

pageScriptsDisabled.description:
The ids of the plugins whose page scripts do not run in the views (RB-060-12); the
window offers the plugins that have page scripts.

items.description: A plugin id: lower-case words joined by `-` (`overlay-grid`).

panelsHidden.description:
The ids of the plugins whose panels the shell does not offer (RB-060-12); the window
offers the plugins that have panels.

showBundled.description: List the plugins that ship with rBrowser in Settings > Plugins (RB-080-51).

lighthouseAnyUrl.description:
Let plugins run Lighthouse on any address. Off holds a run a plugin starts to the sites
the views show, so it cannot read local or LAN pages through Lighthouse's report
(RB-090-21).

consentProbeAnyUrl.description:
Let the consent probe of a plugin granted `consent-probe` load any address. Off holds it
to public addresses and the trusted project's own sites, so a plugin cannot run its
script in a local or LAN page (RB-094-09).

panelMessageMaxBytes.description:
The largest message between a plugin panel and rBrowser, as JSON text in bytes, in
either direction (RB-090-44): a call's arguments, its answer, an event. A page script's
messages keep their own 64 KiB.

checkOnStart.description:
Look for updates of the plugins installed from the catalogue at every start, and say so
in the status bar when there are some.

items.description: A plugin repository a person added to the catalogue.

url.description: The https address of the repository's `rbrowser-plugin-index.json`.

publicKey.description: The repository's Ed25519 public key, base64 (as `rb-plugin-pack keygen` prints it).

repositories.description:
Plugin repositories besides the official catalogue: each an https address of its
`rbrowser-plugin-index.json` and the public key its index is signed with.

autoUpdate.description:
Install an update of a plugin by itself when the update check finds one that is signed
by the same key and asks for nothing more (RB-091-04); one that asks for more waits for a
click in the catalogue.

preferRepository.description:
Install a chosen first-party plugin from the official repository when it offers the
bundled version or a newer one (RB-091-04); off, every chosen plugin comes from the
bundle beside rBrowser and nothing reaches the network.

missingNotice.description:
Say in the status bar when the project's config names a plugin that is not installed
(RB-091-04).

newNotice.description:
Name the plugins new in rBrowser's bundle once after the update that brought them, with
a button that installs them (RB-094-13).

catalog.description: The plugin catalogue (RB-091-01): Settings > Plugins > Catalog.

plugins.description: Settings > Plugins (RB-010-03); every key that widens a plugin is protected from MCP.

persistSessionCookies.description:
Session cookies (logins without an expiry) are written to disk and survive a restart, in
every session. Off, they end with the app as in a browser. Read when rBrowser starts.

stateExportAllDomains.description:
`session.state_export` writes the cookies and storage of every domain in the session's
jar. Off, only those of the project's environments and start URL (RB-094-08). A login
state file is a secret; only a person widens it.

sessions.description: Security > Sessions: whether session cookies outlive the app (RB-020-07).

helperPath.description:
Another rbrowser-wsl helper than the one in the package, as a Linux path or a Windows
path; empty for the packaged one.

distro.description:
The WSL distribution the helper runs in; empty for the project's distribution, else WSL's
default.

networkingModeOverride.description: The WSL networking mode: detected (auto), or mirrored or NAT set by hand.

wsl.description:
Reload & Files > WSL watcher and the WSL networking mode (RB-030-04, read as
`rb_wsl::settings::WslSettings`).

ffmpegPath.description:
An ffmpeg of your own: the absolute path of the program. Empty uses the LGPL build
rBrowser downloads when you run "Video: download ffmpeg".

cloudflaredPath.description:
A cloudflared of your own for the portal's presentation over the internet (RB-096-05):
the absolute path of the program. Empty uses the build rBrowser downloads after you agreed.

tools.description: Capture > Video: an ffmpeg of the user's own, never a project's (RB-080-02).

followEnvironment.description:
A page that lies under an environment of the project is bookmarked as its path
(`/shop/cart?x=1#top`), so the bookmark opens on whichever environment is in effect; a
page of a foreign host stays an absolute URL. Off, every new bookmark is an absolute URL.

bookmarks.description: Project > bookmarks: whether a new bookmark follows the environment (RB-080-48).

dock.description:
Where the plugin panels show: docked `right` (the default), `left` or `bottom` in the
main window, where the views make room, or `floating` in a window of their own. The dock
commands and the Dock menu in the panels' header set it.

left.description: The width of the panels docked left of the views, in DIP.

right.description: The width of the panels docked right of the views, in DIP.

bottom.description: The height of the panels docked below the views, in DIP.

dockSize.description: The docked panels' size per side, in DIP.

oneOf.description: Open at their size (in their own window: the window is open).

dockState.description:
The docked panels now: `open` at their size, `rail` folded to the icon rail (the header
below the views, the icon column beside them) so the views get the room, or `hidden`.
The expand and collapse buttons, a panel icon in the rail, Close and
`panels.dock.toggle` set it (RB-080-93).

sidebar.description:
The panels' side bar: `expanded` shows icons with titles, `icons` only the icons, with
the title as a tooltip (RB-080-61). A narrow dock shows only icons either way.

oneOf.description: As they were left: open, the rail or hidden.

dockAtStart.description:
How the docked panels start: `rail` folded to the icon rail (the default), `hidden`, or
`last` as they were left (RB-080-93). Panels in their own window start at the rail.

closeTo.description:
What Close does to the panels (the X in their header, `panels.close`, closing their own
window): `rail` folds them to the icon rail (the default), `hidden` hides them
(RB-080-93).

keepFrames.description:
How many of the panels shown last stay loaded, hidden, beside the shown one, so
switching back to one does not load it again (RB-090-38); `0` loads each panel anew.

panels.description: Plugins > Installed: the plugin panels floating or docked in the window (RB-080-57).

wheel.description:
Ctrl and the mouse wheel over a page zoom it, as in Chromium. Off, rBrowser puts a
zoom the wheel made back at once; only the keys, the commands and MCP zoom.

sync.description:
A page zoom applies to every view at once, wherever it was made. Off, it is the view's
own - except that Chromium keeps the zoom per site: views of one session showing the
same host zoom together, and each one's badge says so.

keepOnReload.description:
A zoomed page keeps its zoom when it reloads or navigates, as Chromium keeps it per
site. Off, every load starts at 100 %.

pageZoom.description: The page zoom inside a view (RB-090-20).

views.description: Layout > zoom: the page zoom inside a view (RB-090-20).

galleryOpensIn.description: Where the gallery of a capture opens: a window of rBrowser's own or the system browser.

sitemap.description: Capture > Sitemap: where a capture's gallery opens (RB-090-83).

folder.description:
The folder a bug report is written into, each in a folder of its own named by the time;
empty: the project's `.rbrowser/out/reports/`. An absolute path of an existing folder.

preview.description:
Show the report's texts after masking before it is saved, with Save and Cancel; a
cancelled report leaves nothing behind.

report.description: Capture > Bug report: the report's folder and the preview (RB-093-04).

description: The whole user settings file. Every section defaults.
title: UserSettings
